source.title: Tracr: Compiled Transformers as a Laboratory for Interpretability
source.authors: David Lindner; J'anos Kram'ar; Sebastian Farquhar; Matthew Rahtz; Tom McGrath; Vladimir Mikulik

record.tranche_reason: The study examines superposition in compiled transformer models using a gradient-trained compression procedure, a different method from the cited superposition work.
record.gate_note: The frac_prevs compression experiment reports feature-embedding overlap and non-orthogonal representations, which bear on V3. Performance and layer-cosine results for sort_unique are not measurements of polysemanticity or feature packing, so they are not rows. The discussion of Tracr as a testbed and results cited from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: This does not test any version. Tracr is a compiler paper, and superposition is a case study. The study forces superposition by learning a projection that shrinks the residual stream of hand-compiled models (D=14 to d=8). It then inspects how residual-stream feature directions overlap. It never measures whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs. The overlap is induced on purpose by the compression, not observed arising in normally trained networks. Under the rules, a deliberately induced effect on a related construct (residual directions, not neurons) goes in fits_no_version, not counted as a test of V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors present compression of Tracr models as a way to study superposition in multi-step transformers. They say it confirms Elhage et al. (2022b) in a new setting: unnecessary features are dropped and less important features are held in superposition. They add that redundant variables share embedding space. They caution that compressed models may use different encodings, e.g. numerical target_pos in sort_unique, so the compiled program no longer serves as exact ground truth.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a shared learned linear projection to compress compiled multi-step transformer models, with other weights frozen and losses on outputs and layer activations; it is not an explicit replication of the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Compression dimension affects task performance; the study reports that reducing frac_prevs below about d = 6 worsens performance. The reported internal representation also differs between frac_prevs and sort_unique.

fits_no_version.finding: frac_prevs was compressed by a learned shared projection from D=14 to d=8, with other weights frozen. In the result, task-unneeded token features are dropped, and crucial features (tokens:x, is_x, frac_prevs) mostly get their own dimensions. The sparse, non-co-occurring indices embeddings sit in non-orthogonal dimensions. The redundant is_x and tokens:x share part of the space. Performance holds down to about d=6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: When a transformer's residual stream is forced to compress, it drops unneeded features and stores sparse, less important or redundant features in superposition (non-orthogonal residual directions).

record.problems: The evidence comes from deliberately compressed, hand-compiled algorithmic models, not naturally trained language or vision models. The study reports qualitative feature-overlap findings without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: The frac_prevs task-performance result at d = 6 and sort_unique accuracy and layer-cosine results in Figures 7–8 were not included as rows because they do not measure polysemanticity or feature packing. The paper states that frac_prevs performance is not hurt at d = 6 and that sort_unique can achieve almost perfect accuracy while layer cosine similarity stays around 0.8.

untested.parts: No vision models or neuron response analysis.
No trained language-model MLP neuron survey.
No measurement of neuron polysemanticity, and no causal link from feature count to polysemantic neurons in trained networks. Superposition is forced in residual dimensions only.
No comparison of activation function, architecture or regularization.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V3 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are removed. The evidence concerns induced residual-stream superposition in hand-compiled models, not polysemantic neurons. The paper is NeurIPS 2023, and code is released. It is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier or vision neuron response analysis.
No language-model MLP neuron survey across tokens, contexts, or layers.

Tests compression-induced feature overlap in compiled algorithmic transformers, not whether naturally trained networks generally develop polysemantic neurons because they represent more sparse features than neurons.
No test of polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.
No comparison of activation functions, architectures, or regularization effects on polysemanticity.
No analysis of whether apparently mixed neuron responses resolve into a shared feature or related jobs.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods for classifying neurons as polysemantic.

rows.subject: frac_prevs compressed model
rows.operation_detail: Trained a shared linear projection to compress the compiled model, freezing other weights.
rows.baseline: The compiled model has disentangled, orthogonal feature subspaces.
rows.value: The embeddings of is_x and tokens:x share part of the embedding space; indices embeddings are stored in non-orthogonal dimensions.
rows.note: The authors say is_x and tokens:x encode similar information. They describe the non-orthogonal indices embeddings as consistent with superposition because the indices are sparse and do not occur together.
rows.check: The row reports overlapping and non-orthogonal residual-stream feature embeddings (Figure 7c, W^T W) after compression that is forced by design. It does not measure neuron polysemanticity, and it does not show that polysemantic neurons are caused by packing sparse features. So it does not bear on V3 as worded. Keep it as a superposition-geometry observation under fits_no_version. The observation itself, non-orthogonal storage of sparse indices embeddings, is reported as stated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The compressed representation places some feature embeddings in shared or non-orthogonal dimensions, as reported in R1.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported overlap between is_x and tokens:x is attributed to shared information, and the result is from deliberately compressed compiled models rather than naturally trained networks; see R1.
